title: Sidekick's continual learning loop
gist: Shopify mines low-scoring production conversations from its store agent, repairs them with a panel of frontier models, and trains a smaller model on the repaired runs, first by imitation and then by reinforcement learning against a calibrated judge. The pipeline and a full fine-tune run daily. It also trained a short sequence of learned tokens to stand in for a 6,000-token system prompt.
changes: A product replaced a frontier model with a smaller one it retrains every day from its own failures, and trained part of the prompt into the weights to serve it faster. Both are training done for serving: one for the task, one for the cost of every request.
caveats: Shopify's own figures. The 96% saving is estimated from average token prices, not measured spend, and the quality lead over the frontier model is asserted without a number. The page shows only an update date. How new weights reach production is not described, and the agent serves one narrow job, writing queries against its own API.
